# Genres: what players expect, and which blocks fit

Pick the genre first, then the blocks. A game says its genre once, in `money.genre` (`gp explain money.genre`): the money model benchmarks it with the genre's CrazyGames numbers, and the genre says what its players come for, what they expect to find (the must-haves) and which runtime blocks fit it. Some blocks only make sense in one genre — offline earnings, prestige, several sites with a map are idle mechanics — and are not offered to every game.

- `gp catalog genres` — the table below; `gp explain genre.<id>` — one genre (`gp explain genres` lists them);
- `gp catalog blocks --genre <id>` — the blocks that fit, its own first; `gp catalog blocks` — every block and its genres;
- `money.genre` and `gp forecast --idea --genre <id>` take a sub-genre too (benchmarked as its genre); the idea forecast prints the must-haves;
- `gp validate` (a `kit: code` game) reads the names its source imports from `@gp/*`: **I_GENRE_EXPECTS** (a hint) lists the genre's must-haves it doesn't seem to have (no block imported, no sign of its own code for it, nothing in the money design); **W_GENRE_BLOCK** warns about a block of another genre (`offlineEarnings` in an action game). The YAML kits bring their genre with them (kids, hypercasual).

The registry is `packages/spec/src/genres.ts`: the genres are the money genres of `packages/spec/src/money.ts`, each sub-genre maps onto one. A new genre, sub-genre or must-have goes there, with the blocks that serve it; `gp docs` regenerates this page.

## `puzzle` — Puzzle

Players come for a clear rule and levels that get harder, solved at their own pace — the longest sessions on CrazyGames. Benchmarks: `genre.puzzle.minutes`, `genre.puzzle.d1`, `genre.puzzle.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/upgrades.md#1-pick-a-shape (levels and stars), docs/guides/code-games.md.

**Players expect:**

- levels opened in order, a level select to come back to — `levelOpen`, `firstOpenLevel`
- 1–3 stars for solving a level well (a par) — `recordStars`, `starsFromPar`, `loadStars`
- undo and restart a level without penalty — `UndoHistory`
- a hint when stuck (a rewarded "Stuck?" panel); or a rewarded offer of kind hint

**Blocks that fit:** `levelOpen` (@gp/core), `firstOpenLevel` (@gp/core), `loadStars` (@gp/core), `recordStars` (@gp/core), `starsFromPar` (@gp/core), `UndoHistory` (@gp/core), `Tiers` (@gp/core), `daySeed` (@gp/core), `recordDaily` (@gp/core), `physicsAfterInit` (@gp/physics), `StoryRunner` (@gp/core), `dailyTable` (@gp/core/daily-table), `shareCode` (@gp/core/share), `Board` (@gp/core), `Dice` (@gp/core); and those of every genre.

## `idle` — Idle / incremental

Players come for a number that keeps growing, a purchase every minute, and something earned while away. Benchmarks: `genre.idle.minutes`, `genre.idle.d1`, `genre.idle.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/upgrades.md#4-the-math-of-a-level-shop.

Sub-genres (`money.genre` takes them): `clicker` — a tap that pays, then automation that pays more; `incremental` — new layers that open as the numbers grow; `tycoon` — a business that grows from one site to many: managers, upgrades, a map of places; `merge` — two of a kind become the next, a board that fills, a collection of every tier.

**Players expect:**

- a number that keeps growing: a currency in big, readable numbers — `formatAmount`, `UpgradeShop`
- a level shop: dozens of levels, ×10 / Max, milestones — `UpgradeShop`, `mountUpgradeShop`
- offline earnings: what it made while the player was away, ×2 for an ad — `offlineEarnings`
- prestige: a reset for a permanent multiplier (after the first session) — `Prestige`
- *Tycoon* also: several places (sites) to open, each with its own upgrades, on a map (`Sites`, `mountSitesMap`)
- *Merge* also: a collection of every tier reached (`Tiers`, `Roster`)

**Blocks that fit:** `UpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `mountUpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `formatAmount` (@gp/core), `offlineEarnings` (@gp/core, idle only), `Prestige` (@gp/core, idle only), `Sites` (@gp/core, idle only), `mountSitesMap` (@gp/core, idle only), `Tiers` (@gp/core), `readout` (@gp/art/hud), `StoryRunner` (@gp/core), `seasonPass` (@gp/core), `mountSeasonTrack` (@gp/core), `weeklyEvent` (@gp/core), `worldClock` (@gp/core/clock), `restockShop` (@gp/core/restock), `mountRestockTimer` (@gp/core), `LootTable` (@gp/core/loot), `variants` (@gp/core/variants); and those of every genre.

## `action` — Action

Players come for a hook in seconds, runs that escalate to a peak, and a meta that makes the next run different — the best D1 on CrazyGames. Benchmarks: `genre.action.minutes`, `genre.action.d1`, `genre.action.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/upgrades.md#1-pick-a-shape.

Sub-genres (`money.genre` takes them): `roguelite` — a run that is different every time, a build made in the run, and a meta that carries over; `survivors` — a swarm that grows, weapons that fire on their own, a level-up every half minute; `platformer` — tight controls, levels to clear, collectibles that show how well.

**Players expect:**

- meta progression between runs, in the genre's shape: unlocks that play differently, tiers, pacts — `Roster`, `Tiers`, `PactTree`, `UpgradeShop`
- a peak every few minutes: a boss or a wave with a new rule — `BossPatterns`
- a second chance: a revive or a continue (once a session); or a rewarded offer of kind revive / continue
- *Roguelite* also: a run seed: see it, copy it, type it back; a daily run (`seedField`, `newRunSeed`, `runSeedFrom`, `dailyRunSeed`); run choices: pick 1 of 3 at a level-up or a floor, a reroll (`RunChoices`)
- *Survivors-like* also: a pick of 1 of 3 upgrades at every level-up (`RunChoices`)
- *Platformer* also: levels opened in order, with stars or collectibles (`levelOpen`, `recordStars`)

**Blocks that fit:** `Roster` (@gp/core), `Tiers` (@gp/core), `PactTree` (@gp/core), `RunChoices` (@gp/core), `UpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `MoveInput` (@gp/core), `Camera` (@gp/art/camera), `physicsAfterInit` (@gp/physics), `StoryRunner` (@gp/core), `seasonPass` (@gp/core), `mountSeasonTrack` (@gp/core), `weeklyEvent` (@gp/core), `LootTable` (@gp/core/loot), `worldClock` (@gp/core/clock), `TwinStick` (@gp/core), `LookInput` (@gp/core), `aimAssist` (@gp/core), `steer` (@gp/core), `BossPatterns` (@gp/core), `callouts` (@gp/core), `HitArcs` (@gp/art/hud), `DamageNumbers` (@gp/art/hud), `edgeArrow` (@gp/art/hud), `QualityLadder` (@gp/core); and those of every genre.

## `shooting` — Shooting

Players come for weapons that feel different, enemies in waves, hits that land. Benchmarks: `genre.shooting.minutes`, `genre.shooting.d1`, `genre.shooting.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/upgrades.md#1-pick-a-shape.

**Players expect:**

- weapons that play differently, unlocked between runs — `Roster`, `Tiers`
- escalating waves and a boss — `BossPatterns`

**Blocks that fit:** `Roster` (@gp/core), `Tiers` (@gp/core), `UpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `RunChoices` (@gp/core), `TwinStick` (@gp/core), `LookInput` (@gp/core), `aimAssist` (@gp/core), `steer` (@gp/core), `BossPatterns` (@gp/core), `HitArcs` (@gp/art/hud), `DamageNumbers` (@gp/art/hud), `edgeArrow` (@gp/art/hud), `callouts` (@gp/core), `QualityLadder` (@gp/core), `MoveInput` (@gp/core), `Camera` (@gp/art/camera); and those of every genre.

## `strategy` — Strategy / tower defense

Players come for a plan that pays off: build choices with a cost, stages to clear well, a harder tier after the campaign. Benchmarks: `genre.strategy.minutes`, `genre.strategy.d1`, `genre.strategy.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/upgrades.md#1-pick-a-shape (Dread Throne).

Sub-genres (`money.genre` takes them): `tower-defense` — towers that counter enemies, waves to read, stages with stars; `deckbuilder` — a deck that grows in the run — cards drafted after each fight or round, removed and upgraded — fights that are puzzles because the enemy shows its next move, and a play whose outcome they can read before they commit it.

**Players expect:**

- choices with a cost: pacts, forks, tiers — `PactTree`, `Tiers`
- stages with stars, opened in order — `levelOpen`, `recordStars`
- *Tower defense* also: waves announced ahead, so the player can plan
- *Deckbuilder* also: a card draft: pick 1 of 3 after a fight or a round, with a reroll or a skip (`RunChoices`); the deck on view: the draw and discard piles, cards removed and upgraded (a thin deck is a choice) (`Zones`); the outcome before the commit: what a play will score or deal, on the card or the board ("how much will I get?" — Velvet Domino Rogue's players); the enemy's next move shown before it acts (its intent) (`Automa`); a run seed and a daily run: the same deal for everyone (`seedField`, `newRunSeed`, `runSeedFrom`, `dailyRunSeed`)

**Blocks that fit:** `PactTree` (@gp/core), `Tiers` (@gp/core), `UpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `levelOpen` (@gp/core), `recordStars` (@gp/core), `RunChoices` (@gp/core), `dailyTable` (@gp/core/daily-table), `rivals` (@gp/core/rivals), `Board` (@gp/core), `Automa` (@gp/core), `Zones` (@gp/core), `Dice` (@gp/core); and those of every genre.

## `io` — .io

Players come for other players (or bots that pass for them) in a round, a rank, instant respawn, skins to unlock. Benchmarks: `genre.io.minutes`, `genre.io.d1`, `genre.io.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: AGENTS.md §5 (portal multiplayer services are a known gap).

**Players expect:**

- a rank or leaderboard inside the round
- skins or classes to unlock — `Roster`

**Blocks that fit:** `Roster` (@gp/core), `MoveInput` (@gp/core), `Camera` (@gp/art/camera); and those of every genre.

## `driving` — Driving

Players come for cars to unlock and tune, tracks to beat, a race that ends in 2–3 minutes. Benchmarks: `genre.driving.minutes`, `genre.driving.d1`, `genre.driving.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/upgrades.md#1-pick-a-shape.

**Players expect:**

- cars to unlock and upgrade — `Roster`, `UpgradeShop`
- tracks or levels with stars or medals — `levelOpen`, `recordStars`

**Blocks that fit:** `Roster` (@gp/core), `UpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `levelOpen` (@gp/core), `recordStars` (@gp/core), `MoveInput` (@gp/core), `Camera` (@gp/art/camera), `physicsAfterInit` (@gp/physics), `shareCode` (@gp/core/share), `rivals` (@gp/core/rivals), `dailyTable` (@gp/core/daily-table); and those of every genre.

## `hypercasual` — Hypercasual

Players come for one action, a short round, a best to beat and Play again at once — the shortest sessions: add a reason to come back. Benchmarks: `genre.hypercasual.minutes`, `genre.hypercasual.d1`, `genre.hypercasual.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/game-design.md#web-portals-crazygames-13-what-players-stay-for.

**Players expect:**

- Play again at once: the next run is the big button — `mountResults`
- a best score or time to beat, kept between visits

**Blocks that fit:** `UpgradeShop` (@gp/core), `dailyRunSeed` (@gp/core/seed), `recordDaily` (@gp/core), `dailyTable` (@gp/core/daily-table), `rivals` (@gp/core/rivals); and those of every genre.

## `kids` — Kids (Google Play Families)

Players come for a child: big targets, a voice, a reward after every round, never a loss — the kids kit has all of it. Benchmarks: `genre.kids.minutes`, `genre.kids.d1`, `genre.kids.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/game-design.md#children-audiences-ages-.

## `other` — Other (genre unknown)

Players come for nothing the platform can name: set money.genre, and the benchmarks and the must-haves follow. Benchmarks: `genre.other.minutes`, `genre.other.d1`, `genre.other.breakEvery` (MONEY_TABLE). More: docs/guides/genres.md.
